obligations.note: The approved catalog at base sets the auto-approve DTI limit at 40% (params.dti_max_percent = 40), and the change does not amend it. Head code sets Policy.DTI_MAX_PERCENT to 43 and edits controls/mortgage/policy-params.json to 43, so the code no longer equals the approved value; the credit-committee minutes CP-2026-31 are cited but not in the packet.

Ledger entry ACR-0406 (CRD-1) covers Policy.java DTI_MAX_PERCENT, which this change alters, so it has lapsed. The 'renewed' proof names the head commit but keeps the premise DTI_MAX_PERCENT = 40, which is false at head, so it is not valid replacement evidence.
The change deviates from CRD-1's approved 40% DTI limit. The register has no exception for CRD-1 or mortgage.underwriting/policy.

Ticket CHG-25598 is standard and approved by change manager erik.brandt on 2026-10-05, before the PR opened. Its components (mortgage.controls-data, mortgage.policy, mortgage.tests) cover all three touched paths.
The code_review approval comes from wen.li, a change_approver for baseline-mortgage and a different person from the author declan.farrell.
Both approvals name head commit 841b407, which is the only commit on the change.

run.json shows success on head 841b407 with 124 tests, 0 failed or skipped, including the registered exhaustive CRD-1 control test UnderwritingControlTest#autoApproveGridMatchesPolicy. That test passing against the edited params file does not cure the CRD-1 violation.
The change touches protected path controls/mortgage/policy-params.json. It has a control_owner approval from bao.tran (controls-office, outside the author's lending-eng team) on the head commit.

summary: The change raises the auto-approve DTI ceiling from 40% to 43% in both code and the params file. The bank's approved obligation catalog still states the approved limit is 40%, so CRD-1 is violated, and no exception covers the deviation. The prior CRD-1 evidence lapsed, and the replacement proof is invalid because its premise (DTI = 40) contradicts the head code. The process records (ticket, independent review, control-owner approval, CI on head) are in order, but the product obligation is refuted, so the change is rejected until the approved catalog value is formally changed.
